audit_diagnostics.interpretation: The zero HT estimate is not surprising under this sparse heavy-tail regime. A 20% uniform audit floor maintains nonzero support but is too sparse for reliable one-batch detection or calibration when only three rejected cases carry all missed gain.

oracle.endpoint_local_exhaustive_truth: pass for natural, two-arm final, exhaustive challenger best, v1 output, v2 output, fixed64 output, and fixed128 output in all 40 cases

interpretation.primary: The v2 audit layer did not improve quality on this realized holdout because all three audited rejected branches had zero missed gain. It spent extra compute while preserving the incumbent safety invariant. The predeclared weak usefulness rule technically passed because v2 matched v1 gain at 20.13% of exhaustive compute, but this is not evidence that 20% auditing is adequate for tail detection.
interpretation.late_tail: Three quartic beneficial cases rejected at index 65 had gaps 23,24,28 and did not first beat the incumbent until indices 300,390,575. Prefix closeness is therefore not even qualitatively necessary for eventual large benefit at this scale.
interpretation.monitoring: Known nonzero propensity is still useful for future off-policy estimation, but reliable monitoring needs accumulation across more tasks, risk-stratified auditing, or anytime-valid inference rather than expecting a 40-case batch with p=0.2 to expose rare tail benefits.
